audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 6 draft aligned to guilt offering, cow/cart test, ark return, Beth-shemesh offering and deaths, and Kiriath-jearim request; maximum textual audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: Ark of YHWH was in field of Philistines seven months.

familiar.text: And the ark of the LORD was in the country of the Philistines seven months.

modern.text: When the ark of the LORD had been in the land of the Philistines seven months,

original.text: וַיְהִ֧י אֲרוֹן יְהוָ֛ה בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Philistines called for priests and diviners, saying, What shall we do with ark of YHWH? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place.

familiar.text: And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, What shall we do to the ark of the LORD? tell us wherewith we shall send it to his place.

modern.text: the Philistines summoned the priests and diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back to its place.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְלַקֹּֽסְמִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַֽה נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה הוֹדִעֻ֕נוּ בַּמֶּ֖ה נְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ

verses.restored: They said, If you send away ark of God of Israel, do not send it empty, but returning, return to him a guilt offering. Then you may be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand does not turn aside from you.

familiar.text: And they said, If ye send away the ark of the God of Israel, send it not empty; but in any wise return him a trespass offering: then ye shall be healed, and it shall be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.

modern.text: They replied, “If you return the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אִֽם מְשַׁלְּחִ֞ים אֶת אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַל תְּשַׁלְּח֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ רֵיקָ֔ם כִּֽי הָשֵׁ֥ב תָּשִׁ֛יבוּ ל֖וֹ אָשָׁ֑ם אָ֤ז תֵּרָֽפְאוּ֙ וְנוֹדַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה לֹא תָס֥וּר יָד֖וֹ מִכֶּֽם

verses.restored: They said, What guilt offering shall we return to him? They said, According to number of lords of Philistines: five golden tumors and five golden mice, for one plague is upon all of you and upon your lords.

familiar.text: Then said they, What shall be the trespass offering which we shall return to him? They answered, Five golden emerods, and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines: for one plague was on you all, and on your lords.

modern.text: “What guilt offering should we send back to Him?” asked the Philistines. “Five gold tumors and five gold rats,” they said, “according to the number of rulers of the Philistines, since the same plague has struck both you and your rulers.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מָ֣ה הָאָשָׁם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָשִׁ֣יב לוֹ֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מִסְפַּר֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עפלי זָהָ֔ב וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה עַכְבְּרֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב כִּֽי מַגֵּפָ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לְכֻלָּ֖ם וּלְסַרְנֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: You shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that ruin land, and give glory to God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand from upon you, your gods, and your land.

familiar.text: Wherefore ye shall make images of your emerods, and images of your mice that mar the land; and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel: peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.

modern.text: Make images of your tumors and of the rats that are ravaging the land. Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.

original.text: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֩ צַלְמֵ֨י עפליכם וְצַלְמֵ֣י עַכְבְּרֵיכֶ֗ם הַמַּשְׁחִיתִם֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּנְתַתֶּ֛ם לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּב֑וֹד אוּלַ֗י יָקֵ֤ל אֶת יָדוֹ֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אַרְצְכֶֽם

verses.restored: Why should you make your hearts heavy as Egyptians and Pharaoh made their hearts heavy? Was it not after he dealt severely with them that they sent them away and they went?

familiar.text: Wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? when he had wrought wonderfully among them, did they not let the people go, and they departed?

modern.text: Why harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? When He afflicted them, did they not send the people on their way as they departed?

original.text: וְלָ֤מָּה תְכַבְּדוּ֙ אֶת לְבַבְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר כִּבְּד֛וּ מִצְרַ֥יִם וּפַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת לִבָּ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְעַלֵּ֣ל בָּהֶ֔ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּם וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ

verses.restored: Now take and make one new cart, and two milk cows upon whom no yoke has gone up. Bind cows to cart, and return their calves home from behind them.

familiar.text: Now therefore make a new cart, and take two milch kine, on which there hath come no yoke, and tie the kine to the cart, and bring their calves home from them:

modern.text: Now, therefore, prepare one new cart with two milk cows that have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְח֨וּ וַעֲשׂ֜וּ עֲגָלָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא עָלָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֹ֑ל וַאֲסַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת הַפָּרוֹת֙ בָּעֲגָלָ֔ה וַהֲשֵׁיבֹתֶ֧ם בְּנֵיהֶ֛ם מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּֽיְתָה

verses.restored: Take ark of YHWH and put it upon cart. Put vessels of gold that you return to him as guilt offering in box at its side, send it, and let it go.

familiar.text: And take the ark of the LORD, and lay it upon the cart; and put the jewels of gold, which ye return him for a trespass offering, in a coffer by the side thereof; and send it away, that it may go.

modern.text: Take the ark of the LORD, set it on the cart, and in a chest beside it put the gold objects you are sending Him as a guilt offering. Then send the ark on its way,

original.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֶת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל הָ֣עֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֵ֣ת כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶ֥ם לוֹ֙ אָשָׁ֔ם תָּשִׂ֥ימוּ בָאַרְגַּ֖ז מִצִּדּ֑וֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ וְהָלָֽךְ

verses.restored: Watch: if it goes up by way of its territory to Beth-shemesh, he has done to us this great evil. But if not, then we will know that it was not his hand that struck us; by chance it happened to us.

familiar.text: And see, if it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Bethshemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that smote us: it was a chance that happened to us.

modern.text: but keep watching it. If it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh, it is the LORD who has brought on us this great disaster. But if it does not, then we will know that it was not His hand that punished us and that it happened by chance.”

original.text: וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם אִם דֶּ֨רֶךְ גְּבוּל֤וֹ יַֽעֲלֶה֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ ה֚וּא עָ֣שָׂה לָ֔נוּ אֶת הָרָעָ֥ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את וְאִם לֹ֗א וְיָדַ֨עְנוּ֙ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדוֹ֙ נָ֣גְעָה בָּ֔נוּ מִקְרֶ֥ה ה֖וּא הָ֥יָה לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: Humans did so. They took two milk cows, bound them to cart, and shut their calves in house.

familiar.text: And the men did so; and took two milch kine, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home:

modern.text: So the men did as instructed. They took two milk cows, hitched them to the cart, and penned up their calves.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְח֗וּ שְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת וַיַּאַסְר֖וּם בָּעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֶת בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּל֥וּ בַבָּֽיִת

verses.restored: They set ark of YHWH upon cart, and box with golden mice and images of their tumors.

familiar.text: And they laid the ark of the LORD upon the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the images of their emerods.

modern.text: Then they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, along with the chest containing the gold rats and the images of the tumors.

original.text: וַיָּשִׂ֛מוּ אֶת אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה אֶל הָעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֵ֣ת הָאַרְגַּ֗ז וְאֵת֙ עַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֵ֖ת צַלְמֵ֥י טְחֹרֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Cows went straight on way toward Beth-shemesh. On one highway they went, lowing as they went, and did not turn right or left. Lords of Philistines walked after them as far as border of Beth-shemesh.

familiar.text: And the kine took the straight way to the way of Bethshemesh, and went along the highway, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them unto the border of Bethshemesh.

modern.text: And the cows headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, staying on that one highway and lowing as they went, never straying to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed behind them to the border of Beth-shemesh.

original.text: וַיִשַּׁ֨רְנָה הַפָּר֜וֹת בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ עַל דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ בִּמְסִלָּ֣ה אַחַ֗ת הָלְכ֤וּ הָלֹךְ֙ וְגָע֔וֹ וְלֹא סָ֖רוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם עַד גְּב֖וּל בֵּ֥ית שָֽׁמֶשׁ

verses.restored: Beth-shemesh was reaping wheat harvest in valley. They lifted their eyes, saw ark, and rejoiced to see it.

familiar.text: And they of Bethshemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley: and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.

modern.text: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley, and when they looked up and saw the ark, they were overjoyed at the sight.

original.text: וּבֵ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ קֹצְרִ֥ים קְצִיר חִטִּ֖ים בָּעֵ֑מֶק וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֶת עֵינֵיהֶ֗ם וַיִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת הָ֣אָר֔וֹן וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֖וּ לִרְאֽוֹת

verses.restored: Cart came into field of Joshua the Beth-shemite and stood there. A great stone was there. They split wood of cart and offered cows as an ascending offering to YHWH.

familiar.text: And the cart came into the field of Joshua, a Bethshemite, and stood there, where there was a great stone: and they clave the wood of the cart, and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the LORD.

modern.text: The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there near a large rock. The people chopped up the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

original.text: וְהָעֲגָלָ֡ה בָּ֠אָה אֶל שְׂדֵ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בֵּֽית הַשִּׁמְשִׁי֙ וַתַּעֲמֹ֣ד שָׁ֔ם וְשָׁ֖ם אֶ֣בֶן גְּדוֹלָ֑ה וַֽיְבַקְּעוּ֙ אֶת עֲצֵ֣י הָעֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֶת הַ֨פָּר֔וֹת הֶעֱל֥וּ עֹלָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Levites took down ark of YHWH and box that was with it, in which were vessels of gold, and set them upon great stone. Humans of Beth-shemesh offered ascending offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to YHWH.

familiar.text: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD, and the coffer that was with it, wherein the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone: and the men of Bethshemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day unto the LORD.

modern.text: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects, and they placed them on the large rock. That day the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.

original.text: וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם הוֹרִ֣ידוּ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת הָאַרְגַּ֤ז אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁר בּ֣וֹ כְלֵֽי זָהָ֔ב וַיָּשִׂ֖מוּ אֶל הָאֶ֣בֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ הֶעֱל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת וַֽיִּזְבְּח֧וּ זְבָחִ֛ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לַֽיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Five lords of Philistines saw and returned to Ekron on that day.

familiar.text: And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.

modern.text: And when the five rulers of the Philistines saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.

original.text: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה סַרְנֵֽי פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים רָא֑וּ וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ עֶקְר֖וֹן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: These are golden tumors that Philistines returned as guilt offering to YHWH: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

familiar.text: And these are the golden emerods which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering unto the LORD; for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Askelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

modern.text: As a guilt offering to the LORD, the Philistines had sent back one gold tumor for each city: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

original.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ טְחֹרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵשִׁ֧יבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אָשָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְאַשְׁדּ֨וֹד אֶחָ֜ד לְעַזָּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לְאַשְׁקְל֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לְגַ֥ת אֶחָ֖ד לְעֶקְר֥וֹן אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: And golden mice were according to number of all cities of Philistines belonging to five lords, from fortified city to village of open country. Great stone upon which they rested ark of YHWH is witness to this day in field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.

familiar.text: And the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fenced cities, and of country villages, even unto the great stone of Abel, whereon they set down the ark of the LORD: which stone remaineth unto this day in the field of Joshua, the Bethshemite.

modern.text: The number of gold rats also corresponded to the number of Philistine cities belonging to the five rulers—the fortified cities and their outlying villages. And the large rock on which they placed the ark of the LORD stands to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.

original.text: וְעַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב מִסְפַּ֞ר כָּל עָרֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לַחֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַסְּרָנִ֔ים מֵעִ֣יר מִבְצָ֔ר וְעַ֖ד כֹּ֣פֶר הַפְּרָזִ֑י וְעַ֣ד אָבֵ֣ל הַגְּדוֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִנִּ֤יחוּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בֵּֽית הַשִּׁמְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: He struck among humans of Beth-shemesh because they looked into/at ark of YHWH; he struck among people seventy humans. The people mourned because YHWH had struck people with a great striking.

familiar.text: And he smote the men of Bethshemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the LORD, even he smote of the people fifty thousand and threescore and ten men: and the people lamented, because the LORD had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.

modern.text: But God struck down some of the people of Beth-shemesh because they looked inside the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck them with a great slaughter.

original.text: וַיַּ֞ךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּעָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּעָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: Humans of Beth-shemesh said, Who is able to stand before YHWH, this holy God? And to whom shall he go up from upon us?

familiar.text: And the men of Bethshemesh said, Who is able to stand before this holy LORD God? and to whom shall he go up from us?

modern.text: The men of Beth-shemesh asked, “Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom should the ark go up from here?”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ מִ֚י יוּכַ֣ל לַעֲמֹ֔ד לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים הַקָּד֖וֹשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְאֶל מִ֖י יַעֲלֶ֥ה מֵעָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: They sent messengers to inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, Philistines have returned ark of YHWH. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.

familiar.text: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kirjathjearim, saying, The Philistines have brought again the ark of the LORD; come ye down, and fetch it up to you.

modern.text: So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim, saying, “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.”

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י קִרְיַת יְעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵשִׁ֤בוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה רְד֕וּ הַעֲל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵיכֶֽם

translation_notes: Philistine priests and diviners are portrayed as genuine advisers within their community. The text need not be read as permission to ridicule non-Israelite religious expertise.
Golden tumors and mice are mimetic guilt offerings. They represent acknowledged harm but are not magical medical treatment or a substitute for public health.
The Egypt comparison belongs to Israelite narrative memory and should not fuel anti-Egyptian racism or simplistic equations between ancient and modern peoples.
The test uses nursing cows separated from calves, then kills the cows as sacrifice. Animal distress is audible in the narrative and must not be romanticized or repeated.
Omens and chance language reflect ancient discernment. They do not provide a safe method for making high-stakes modern decisions.

Beth-shemesh harvesters rejoice, but handling of the ark leads to a difficult death report. Textual witnesses differ dramatically: the Masoretic wording is commonly read as seventy, while other traditions preserve much larger or differently structured numbers.
Verse 19's reason may be looking at or into the ark, and textual details require maximum audit. The deaths cannot be made ethically simple by invoking holiness.
Collective striking of a community must not justify collective punishment, sacred terror, or claims that accidental ritual mistakes deserve death.
The Beth-shemesh question arises from trauma and fear. Holiness should not be taught as Divine hostility toward ordinary human bodies.
Sending the ark to Kiriath-jearim again transfers responsibility; consent and capacity of receiving communities matter.
Gold offered after harm does not restore dead people, heal trauma automatically, or purchase immunity.
Philistine and Israelite communities both respond to uncertainty through religious interpretation; neither should be caricatured as primitive.
safety_note: Do not imitate animal-distressing omen tests, use gold as magical medicine, or justify collective death for ritual error. Do not ridicule Philistine religion or treat uncertain plague language as medical fact. The Beth-shemesh deaths and textual variants require humility, trauma awareness, and rejection of sacred-terror preaching.
